title: Uniform cohomology criterion for constructible reductions with compatible etale origins
statement: For a Noetherian scheme T, a prime l and a finite extension E of Q_l, an object K of the actual completed integral-coefficient derived category has uniformly bounded constructible reduction local models and compatible bounded-below etale origins if and only if its reductions, transported to constant coefficients by the canonical exact restriction, have intrinsically constructible cohomology in one interval [a,b] independent of the positive quotient level. No completeness condition on K is included.

source.place: ## Proof: implicit triangulation needed for the constructible restriction; agent supplement. Stacks Tag 09C3, proetale.tex, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, supplies contextual local models, not this tower-category closure theorem.

proof.text: The forward implication is precisely the common cohomology bound theorem for uniform local models.

For the converse build the canonical strict normalized reduction tower from the fixed evaluation comparison and reduction normalizations; use the existing pbcReductionAdicTower and its canonical coherence laws from LevelwiseAdicTruncations. The current dependency graph permits this import. Exact constant-coefficient restriction commutes with homology and reflects zero objects. Thus the profile supplies normalizedConstructibleTower_local_effectivity with a common interval, yielding uniform local models and bounded constructible etale origins for every level. Transport each local origin through the canonical function/constant realization comparison. Exact etale comparison reflects the lower cohomological bound. Its full faithfulness on bounded-below derived categories lifts each adjacent normalization and its inverse. Faithfulness then verifies the specified compatibility square, giving the compatible witnessed tower. Combining the two implications proves the criterion.
